rules.statement: Don't ask for the body of an accepted ADR to be reworded when a later ADR supersedes part of it; accepted ADRs are immutable except their Status line, which should point to the newer ADR.
rules.why: An accepted ADR records the decision as it was made; later changes are recorded in a new ADR referenced from the old one's Status line.
rules.check: Before reporting stale content in an accepted ADR, check docs/decisions/README.md for the immutability rule and whether the ADR's Status line already references the superseding ADR; only report if the Status line is missing that reference.

rules.statement: An XML doc comment must not make claims about a type's behaviour that other members of the same type contradict, such as saying a secret is never a string while its readers return strings, or calling a file random bytes when callers use its text.
rules.why: An inaccurate comment misleads readers about how data (especially secrets) is handled and can lead a maintainer to misuse it, for example encoding a value twice.
rules.check: Compare the claims in <summary>/<remarks> against the signatures and bodies of the type's members and its callers; flag claims about representation or lifetime the code does not uphold.

rules.statement: Don't return the same value both from inside a catch and again right after the try/catch; restructure so the method has a single return for that case.
rules.why: Duplicate returns make readers check whether the two paths return different things.
rules.check: Look for a catch block ending in `return x;` immediately followed after the try/catch by the same `return x;`.

rules.statement: Report the same misconfiguration with the same wording everywhere it is detected (options validator and library runtime check), with a comment explaining any intentional difference in the rest of the message.
rules.why: Different messages for one condition confuse hosts and library callers, and the strings drift apart.
rules.check: When a diff adds a validation or exception message for a configuration condition, search for other messages reporting the same condition and compare their wording.

rules.statement: Don't suggest sharing a message constant or other internal member across assemblies through InternalsVisibleTo; when the members live in different production assemblies, ask for matching wording instead.
rules.why: Cross-assembly InternalsVisibleTo between production assemblies is banned by the production C# conventions.
rules.check: Before suggesting a shared constant, check whether the two usages are in different production assemblies and whether the member would have to be internal.

rules.statement: A race-handling branch, such as the path where another process moves a file into place first, should be extracted behind a testable seam and covered by a test.
rules.why: A regression in the lost-race branch, such as overwriting the winner's file, causes divergent state that only shows up indirectly and is hard to diagnose.
rules.check: Look for catch/when branches handling concurrent writers (File.Move IOException, file already exists) with no test exercising them.
